chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Bakkar ibn Kardam and more than one (other narrator), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'The delight of my eyes was placed in salat (prayer), and my pleasure in women.'

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: Salat — the ritual Islamic prayer, performed five times daily. For the Prophet, it was not merely an obligation but the source of his deepest delight.
key_terms.جُعِلَ: Was placed/made — in the passive voice, indicating a divine arrangement. It was God who made salat the source of the Prophet's joy.
key_terms.قُرَّةُ عَيْنِي: Delight/coolness of my eye — a classical Arabic idiom for the greatest joy and comfort. 'Coolness of the eye' refers to the soothing relief that comes from seeing what one loves most.
key_terms.لَذَّتِي: My pleasure/delight — a natural human enjoyment, here referring to the Prophet's love for women in a wholesome, marital context.

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say was the delight of his eyes and his pleasure?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) from the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), declares that the Prophet found his deepest spiritual joy and contentment in salat, and his wholesome human pleasure in women. The pairing reflects an Islamic balance between the spiritual and the natural-human dimensions of a noble life. The phrase 'qurrat al-ayn' (coolness/delight of the eye) is a classical Arabic idiom for the deepest joy and comfort, used in the Quran for righteous children and godly deeds.
